studies.Population: Hospital-based RCC cases and RDD healthy controls among non-Hispanic whites in Houston, Texas
studies.Ethnicity Basis: Population imputation: stated Hispanic/Latino population -> Hispanic/Latino
studies.Ethnicity Supporting Text: Because of the small number of minority participants ( n = 91), we limited the analysis to non-Hispanic whites only
studies.Reference: Joint association of genome-wide association study-identified susceptibility loci and dietary patterns in risk of renal cell carcinoma among non-Hispanic whites.
studies.Authors: Melkonian SC, Daniel CR, Hildebrandt MA, Tannir NM, Ye Y, Chow WH, Wood CG, Wu X
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: We used a previously validated modified version of the National Cancer Institute Health Habits and History Questionnaire ( 26 ). This food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) asks participants about their consumption of 165 food and beverage items

sample_size.excerpt: Because of the small number of minority participants ( n = 91), we limited the analysis to non-Hispanic whites only, leaving 1,358 persons (659 cases and 699 controls) for inclusion in the present study.

effect_size.excerpt: Greater adherence to the fruits and vegetables pattern was inversely related to RCC risk in the multivariable-adjusted model (across tertiles, odds ratio (OR) = 1.00 (referent), OR = 0.66 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.49, 0.88), and OR = 0.54 (95% CI: 0.40, 0.73), respectively; P for trend < 0.001), while a higher pattern score for the “American/Western” dietary pattern was significantly associated with a higher risk of RCC in both models (multivariable-adjusted model: OR = 1.00 (referent), OR = 1.53 (95% CI: 1.12, 2.09), and OR = 1.98 (95% CI: 1.47, 2.67), respectively; P for trend < 0.001).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Greater adherence to the fruits and vegetables pattern was inversely related to RCC risk in the multivariable-adjusted model (across tertiles, odds ratio (OR) = 1.00 (referent), OR = 0.66 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.49, 0.88), and OR = 0.54 (95% CI: 0.40, 0.73), respectively; P for trend < 0.001), while a higher pattern score for the “American/Western” dietary pattern was significantly associated with a higher risk of RCC in both models (multivariable-adjusted model: OR = 1.00 (referent), OR = 1.53 (95% CI: 1.12, 2.09), and OR = 1.98 (95% CI: 1.47, 2.67), respectively; P for trend < 0.001).

comparison.excerpt: Tertiles of dietary pattern factor scores were created using the distribution of intake in the controls, by sex, with the first tertile corresponding to the lowest factor score or level of adherence to that dietary pattern.
comparison.location: Methods, Food grouping and dietary pattern analysis, paragraph 5

design.excerpt: In an ongoing case-control study of RCC initiated in Houston, Texas, in 2002, we identified 3 empirically derived dietary patterns

timing.excerpt: RCC patients were drawn from an ongoing case-control study of RCC initiated in Houston, Texas, in 2002 ( 24 ).
